newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 29.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) and Dong Kuk Steel Mill Co Ltd decided to propose buying the Hanbo Steel Co's assets on Monday.

- During Tuesday's special session of the National Assembly, opposition lawmakers continued to attack ruling New Korea Party presidential candidate Lee Hoi-chang for his sons' expemption from mandatory military service due to low wieght.
- Kia Group affilates' unions rejected an agreement which had been accepted by their umbrella organisation stipulating "no labour disputes" for the next three years with the group management.

- Working-level officials from South and North Korea, China and the United States held a meeting in New York on Monday to discuss "logistics" issues for a preliminary four-party meeting slated for August, 5.

- Seoul and tokyo reached an agreement to resume fishing talks early next month, which were suspended after Japan seized five Korean fishing boats for violating questionable territorial waters in June and July, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
